card.profile: The airflare (or air-flare) refers to an acrobatic movement in which the performer rotates the torso around the vertical axis of their body (extending from the head down vertically) whilst simultaneously traveling in a circular path along a plane parallel with the floor. The feet are not allowed to touch the ground during the execution of this move and both hands are used to execute standard airflares.
card.insight: org petition created by Curtis Hedges of the OBS Group to influence the United States Olympic Committee to recognize Pablo Flores, and more recently Lui Guerrero as the first person in history to perform continuous airflares.

lessons.title: Do One Airflare in Only 5 Minutes | Learn Breakdance ASAP

parts.note: Instructor introduces the video objective: learning an airflare in 5 minutes.
Explains prerequisites including upper body strength, leg flexibility, and hand hops.
First minute drill: setting up the stance, turning, pivoting, and kicking.
Adding hand switches and weight transitions while hanging on the supporting arm.
Practicing hip elevation and body alignment at a 45-degree angle in handstand positioning.
Drilling the side-plank arm throw and hand catch mechanics.
Using a hip-height rail for leg swooping and rotational balance practice.
Demonstrating the full airflare execution with key positioning tips.

steps.name: Airflare Setup & Pivot Drill
steps.description: Standing in a wide stance, place the lead hand down, turn, pivot on the lead foot, and kick the opposite leg high.

steps.name: Arm Throw & Catch Drill
steps.description: From a side plank position, jump off the supporting arm while throwing the non-supporting arm over to catch the ground.

steps.name: Rail Swoop Drill
steps.description: Elevate feet on a waist-high rail to simulate hip height while practice swooping the lower leg under and up.

common_mistakes: Letting the lower body get away from the upper body
Shooting the top leg down instead of keeping it elevated over the head
safety: Ensure proper upper body strength (e.g., 25 decline push-ups) to support joint load during arm switches.
lessons.teacher_style: The instructor breaks down the airflare using a timed, 5-minute progression program designed around specific drills and prerequisites. He maintains an energetic, encouraging tone, offering physical cues and structural advice to help students master the move incrementally.
lessons.distinctive_method: Using a hip-height outdoor railing as an assistive prop to isolate and practice the leg swooping trajectory and single-arm weight bearing of an airflare.
what_works: Clear, timed drill-by-drill structure broken into actionable 30-second intervals.
Use of external props (bench/rail) to isolate weight distribution and leg trajectory.
what_hinders: Fast-paced format may leave insufficient time for beginners to internalize complex weight transfers without pausing.
